page.layout: One page of text, cut off at the right edge; a woodcut ornament at the top; large title lines in capitals; a large decorated initial N opening the ode with the text in lines to its right. No margin notes visible.; One page of text in verse, set in parallel: a main column of Latin verse lines with stanza numbers, and a narrow strip at the left edge carrying fragments of text cut off by the scan. Title lines above the verse are printed in capitals and spaced type. Narrow partial text at the far left and right edges belongs to the cut-off margin and is not transcribed.

main_text.head: ODE I.
SPONSA.
main_text.p: I L ego mor talium Falfa cur gaudia: No honore principum Vana capto somnia: Non opes, amentium Ambio deliria: Est meus sponsæ mihi Sponsus vnus omnia. Hic tot anxiè mihi Expetitus seculis, Non vt ante nuntiis, Non vt ante literis Me salutet eminus: 2. Proximi sed proximus Orisipsius fui Osculetur osculis,

page.notes: The text is cut off at the right edge of the scan, so the lines end incomplete; the decorative initial N is only partly legible. The ornament at the top is partly cut. The first line of the ode is "ILego" with the initial I and small capitals as printed. The line "Non honore" is shown as printed; the initial N is a large woodcut letter joined to the first word. The scan is cut off at the right and left edges and at the bottom; partial words there are marked by their visible letters only. Some letters in the verse are doubtful (e.g. "Ierez", "fatentes", "Obonis"), and the left-margin strip shows only fragments of notes that cannot be read.
